content.content: A birth that cannot complete abandons the change it opened — no half-born change is left behind. `deccy new` opens a change through M-jj-new (xmlwqpyr), then writes the skeleton; if the crossing reports no usable id, or the write fails, the invocation abandons that change and refuses, naming the cause.
content.rationale: S5-lifecycle's creation case (vwlrqoxk) is the only bracketed creation, and this fixes what becomes of the change it opens when the birth cannot complete. A write that cannot be completed is S2-write-fail's (tkwuyxux): it refuses and leaves the previous document as it was — but the change the birth just opened is not a previous document, it is a new one the crossing reported, and leaving it would put a change in the graph that no node document names. Abandoning it through M-jj-abandon (urtkpxwv, S3-abandon xllzxxvo) undoes the open (xmlwqpyr) so the graph returns to what it was, and the refusal is built through M-refusal (popowxnw), carrying the abandon's own failure rather than swallowing it. A refused birth that left its change behind is exactly what M-V-new's caller-creates-first story forbids.
